description: Replace the fall-detection dashboard UI with a minimal sitting/standing web app and update the docs. User requirements: 'Make a website as well. Make it minimal and stay away from gradients or weird fonts. Stick with a pretty basic font and it should be like a dashboard showing how long you've been sitting, how long you've been standing, etc'; 'It will include a bunch of health information on the site'; data on how often people sit and stand that can be shared with health providers; the timed calibration sequence with clear instructions on when to leave, come back, walk, stand still and sit. Depends on FEAT-002 and FEAT-003 APIs.
steps: Rewrite dashboard/static/index.html, style.css and app.js (you may split JS into a few files under dashboard/static/ if it stays CSP-compatible: no inline scripts/styles/handlers, no external URLs; check the CSP constant in dashboard/server.py). Single page with a simple top nav (hash routing): Today, History, Health, Share, Calibrate, Sensor.

Visual rules: light theme, flat solid colours only (no CSS gradients anywhere, remove the radial-gradient brand mark), system font stack only (font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; no @font-face, no web fonts, no monospace display fonts except optional tabular-nums), generous whitespace, thin borders, at most one accent colour plus a distinct colour per state (sitting / standing / moving / away). Accessible: semantic headings, labels for inputs, aria-live for the current posture and calibration countdown, colour is never the only signal (text labels on charts/legend), keyboard focus visible, sufficient contrast.

Today page (default): large current state ('Sitting', 'Standing', 'Moving', 'Away', 'Unknown' + reason such as 'Not calibrated - calibrate the room'), confidence, 'Sitting for 23 min' current streak, tiles for Sitting today, Standing today, Moving today, Upright total, Stand hours X / goal, Sit-to-stand transitions, Longest sitting bout; an hourly canvas bar chart (24 bars, stacked sitting vs upright minutes, with axis labels and a text legend); a stand reminder banner when the API reports an active reminder ('You have been sitting for 30 min. Time to stand up for a minute.') with Snooze 10 min, plus an optional browser Notification (ask permission only on a user click) and a short WebAudio beep. Show a clear SYNTHETIC banner whenever the source is simulation, and a 'Replay, not saved' note for replay.
History page: last 7 / 30 days table and simple bar chart of daily sitting vs upright hours, average sitting bout length, transitions per day, stand hours per day (from /api/posture/history).

Health page: concise, factual, non-prescriptive information about prolonged sitting, written as general information, not medical advice. Cite real sources only, as plain text references (no links required to work offline; if links are added they must not load resources): WHO guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour (World Health Organization, 2020): adults should limit sedentary time and replace it with physical activity of any intensity; Dunstan DW et al., 'Breaking up prolonged sitting reduces postprandial glucose and insulin responses', Diabetes Care 2012;35(5):976-983. Show the user's own 7-day averages next to the information (average daily sitting time, average sitting bout, share of hours with a stand break). Include 'Talk to your healthcare provider for advice about your situation.' Do not invent statistics.

Share page: explain what is collected (only time spent sitting/standing/moving/away and reminder responses, stored locally in data/posture.sqlite3, no camera, no audio, nothing sent anywhere automatically), a date range selector, buttons to download CSV and JSON from /api/posture/export, and a print-friendly provider summary (period, daily averages, bouts, transitions, stand hours, method note and disclaimer) using a @media print stylesheet and window.print() bound via addEventListener.

Calibrate page: before starting, show the full planned schedule from session.timeline (GET /api/calibration/state after POST /api/calibration/start, or computed client-side from step_specs + defaults) as a table with clock offsets: e.g. 0:00 Press Start, leave the room (5 s); 0:05 Empty room recorded (21 s, stay out); 0:26 Come back in (5 s); 0:31 Walk back and forth (16 s); 0:47 Stop and stand still (3 s); 0:50 Standing still recorded (21 s); 1:11 Walk to the chair and sit (3 s); 1:14 Sitting recorded (21 s); 1:35 Done - total 1 min 35 s. Inputs for lead-in, grace, transition and step durations (validated, total updates live). A placement name input (existing placement validation). During the run: a big countdown for the current phase, the current instruction, what comes next, a progress bar for the whole run (solid fill, no gradient), and audio cues so the user outside the room knows when to return: a beep at every phase change plus speechSynthesis reading the phase cue (toggle, on by default, tested with a 'Test sound' button that also unlocks audio). Show per-step quality (ok_fraction, failures with the redo button), and when computed: posture self-check accuracy (labelled 'within-calibration check, optimistic'), warnings (e.g. sitting and standing look similar), and Save. Show the active calibration and allow Clear. Use the existing /api/calibration/* routes (start with auto=true, step/start, step/cancel, step/redo, cancel, save, load, clear).

Sensor page: data source controls (serial port picker with 'auto', replay file, simulation scenario incl. desk_day, Stop) using existing /api/ports, /api/replay_files, /api/source, /api/stop; connection status (packets/s, RSSI, data quality, sensor config) from /api/status; a small live motion score chart from /api/series. Drop the fall alert, recording/takes and heatmap UI from the page (backend routes stay).

Update tests/test_dashboard.py UI tests (e.g. test_index_serves_html_with_disclaimer, test_ui_has_alert_simulation_and_export_controls) to the new page: assert the disclaimer, nav sections, calibrate/share/health sections and element ids the JS uses; add a test that no static asset contains 'gradient' or '@font-face' or external URLs.

Update README.md for the pivot: what the app does (sitting/standing time tracker using two ESP32-S3 boards and Wi-Fi CSI, no camera), quick start with the exact live command `make dashboard ARGS="--serial /dev/cu.usbmodem2101"` and the synthetic demo `make dashboard-sim SCENARIO=desk_day`, the default calibration timeline table (when to leave, come back, walk, stand still, sit; total 1 min 35 s), how detection works (motion gating + per-room posture model from calibration, hysteresis), limitations (location dependent, recalibrate when furniture/boards move, still person outside the TX-RX line may read as away, within-calibration self-check is not validated accuracy), data/privacy and export, disclaimer (not a medical device). Note that the current firmware uses ESP-NOW between the two boards (no router) and that no reflash is needed for this version. Keep the firmware and flashing sections. Update the Makefile help comment and pyproject description if they mention fall detection as the product; add a `make app` alias for `make dashboard` only if trivial.
Run `git add -N` on every new file.
acceptance_criteria: grep -ri 'gradient\|@font-face' dashboard/static returns nothing; the only font-family values are the system stack (and optionally ui-monospace for numbers)
node --check passes for every JS file in dashboard/static
GET / serves a page with Today, History, Health, Share, Calibrate and Sensor sections, the not-a-medical-device disclaimer and no external URLs (test passes)

Calibrate page renders the planned timeline with clock offsets and total, and during a run shows a countdown and plays a beep + spoken cue per phase (code path present; manual check described in findings)
README contains the default calibration timeline and the exact live and synthetic commands
verification: for f in dashboard/static/*.js; do node --check "$f"; done

Background smoke run: .venv/bin/python -m dashboard --no-browser --port 8599 --simulate desk_day & then curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8599/ | grep -c 'not a medical device' and curl the static assets, then kill the server
findings: Rewrote dashboard/static/index.html, style.css, app.js (single JS file, hash routing: Today, History, Health, Share, Calibrate, Sensor; light flat theme, system font stack only, no gradients/@font-face/external URLs, no inline scripts/styles/handlers). No backend changes were needed. Actual default calibration timeline from backend build_timeline (settle_s = processing.window_s = 1.0 is added to each recorded step): 00:00 lead_in Leave the room 5 s; 00:05 empty_baseline 21 s; 00:26 grace Come back in 5 s; 00:31 walking 16 s; 00:47 transition 3 s; 00:50 standing_still 21 s; 01:11 transition 3 s; 01:14 sitting 21 s; total 95 s = 1:35. The JS mirrors build_timeline for the pre-start plan (checked with node: identical offsets and total) and shows the server session.timeline during a run. Start = POST /api/calibration/start (auto=true, inputs validated) then POST /api/calibration/step/start. Countdown interpolated client-side from phase.remaining_s (500 ms polling, 200 ms render); WebAudio beep on every phase change plus 3 short ticks in the last 3 s of each phase, speechSynthesis reads phase.cue (toggle on by default; 'Test sound' unlocks audio), done_cue / failure message spoken at run end. Calibration is also polled every 3 s on other pages so cues continue if the user navigates away. Synthetic calibration button (POST /api/simulation/calibrate) only shown when the source is simulation. Tests: replaced test_ui_has_alert_simulation_and_export_controls with test_ui_has_tracker_pages_and_controls and added test_static_assets_are_minimal_and_offline; updated the title assert. make test exit 0; compileall + node --check OK. Smoke test: the run_in_background server command is blocked by the tool sandbox, so the smoke run used werkzeug make_server on 127.0.0.1:8599 in a Python thread with the desk_day simulation: GET / (3 'not a medical device' matches, case-insensitive), static assets 200, /api/posture/today OK, and a full timed calibration over HTTP went through all 8 phases at the expected offsets (5.1, 26.4, 31.4, 47.2, 50.2, 71.6, 74.6, 95.4 s), computed and saved (desk_day is not aligned with the schedule, so it produced the 'sitting and standing look similar' warning and a 56% self-check, which exercises the warnings path). Not verified: rendering, audio and speech in a real browser, and any live-hardware calibration. README rewritten for the pivot (quick start with exact commands, calibration table, detection, limitations, privacy/export, ESP-NOW/no reflash note; fall-detection docs kept under a legacy section; firmware/flashing kept). Makefile help updated and `make app` alias added; pyproject description updated. All files were already intent-to-add in git (no new files created).
